subject.title: fix(kill-tree): verify process group leader before using group kill to prevent gateway SIGTERM (#76259)

question: Should maintainers accept this PR's leader-checked default Unix kill behavior after a rebase that preserves current-main cleanup fixes, or require a narrower caller-only cleanup design instead?
rationale: The code fixes a real gateway SIGTERM class, but it changes shared process-cleanup semantics and now intersects a newer merged Windows cleanup fix, so the permanent behavior needs maintainer ownership after the mechanical conflict is resolved.

options.title: Rebase and accept leader check
options.body: Require a current-main rebase that preserves https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101392 and the newer cleanup state, then review the leader-check behavior as the intended fix for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/76259.

options.title: Narrow to caller audit
options.body: Reject the shared default change and ask for only spawn-site `detached` propagation, reducing default-behavior risk but leaving omitted callers dependent on audits.

options.title: Pause for replacement
options.body: Keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/76259 open and close or replace this branch if maintainers want a different process-cleanup design.

recommendation.title: Rebase and accept leader check
recommendation.body: Require a current-main rebase that preserves https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101392 and the newer cleanup state, then review the leader-check behavior as the intended fix for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/76259.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merger of the intersecting process cleanup fix and likely routing point for deciding whether to accept the compatibility-sensitive behavior after rebase.
